name: MI-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: No polls or expert ratings signal competitiveness
Markets price Republican win near certain
model.rationale: Moolenaar runs in a heavily Republican district with a massive cash advantage and no polling, ratings, or spending suggesting a race; markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance. The forecast stays close to fundamentals, with a slight Democratic shift for the favorable environment.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the main route to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Michigan's 2nd District is a solidly Republican seat, and incumbent John Moolenaar is seeking another term. He holds a large financial edge, with more than $1.9 million on hand compared with roughly $22,000 for Democrat Ben Ambrose, who has raised under $100,000. No outside groups are spending in the race, and no polls or expert ratings are available. Prediction markets give Moolenaar about a 98% chance of winning.

The district's Republican lean of about 15 points, combined with incumbency and the fundraising gap, makes this one of the least competitive House races on the ballot. A favorable national environment for Democrats is the only factor pointing the other way, and it is far from enough to close a gap of this size.
